text.L1: A magnet does not attract every metal. We must test each material.
text.L2: Magnets attract iron, nickel, cobalt, and steels that contain iron.
text.L3: Aluminium, copper and brass are metals, but they are not attracted. Plastic, wood, paper, rubber and glass are not attracted either.
text.L4: So a shiny or metal-looking object is not automatically magnetic.
text.L5: In our example, test the iron tawa, foil, steel spoon and plastic lid one at a time.
text.L6: Record each result, then group the objects as attracted or not attracted.
text.L7: A magnet can act through paper, cloth, glass and water. It can even pull a paper clip through a glass of water.
text.L8: Two steel spoons can behave differently, so testing is the reliable way to sort materials.
